key_insight: Model-free reinforcement learning can learn pulse-level quantum control strategies for indirect manipulation of NV nuclear spins, even in a noisy spin-bath setting without prior system knowledge.
engineering_relevance: This suggests RL may be a practical black-box optimizer for pulse design on NISQ hardware where accurate device models are incomplete or costly to obtain.
method: Simulated state preparation and qubit gate design for indirectly controlled NV nuclear spins.
Modeled the spin-bath with generalized cluster correlation expansion, including magnetic impurities and intra-bath interactions.
Tested RL in minimally observable environments with noisy, sparse rewards and compared against other black-box optimization methods.
evidence_signal: The paper reports a simulation-based evaluation of RL agents under challenging spin-bath dynamics and benchmarked them against state-of-the-art black-box optimizers.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated in simulation, so transfer to real hardware may be limited by model mismatch, measurement sparsity, and reward noise.
paper_title: Quantum control of solid state qubits via Reinforcement Learning
